subject: R-16 historical settlement roster, sixth batch (batch 6)
envelopeRegions: 9 - Levant & Syria (Phoenicia, Judaea, Nabataean fringe) (mid ~40); 10 - Mesopotamia & Babylonia (mid ~31); 11 - Iran & the Iranian plateau (mid ~36)
batchScope: The Levantine and Syrian littoral and interior (Phoenicia, Coele-Syria, Judaea/Samaria, the Decapolis and Transjordan, the Nabataean fringe), Mesopotamia and Babylonia with Assyria and the northern Syrian Euphrates, and the Iranian plateau (Persis, Media, Parthia/Hyrcania, Aria/Drangiana/Arachosia, Carmania, Gedrosia, Elymais/Susiana and Atropatene).
coordinateConvention: WGS84 decimal degrees, approximate representative points for the ancient site (not the modern town unless noted). Precision does not imply archaeological accuracy and is not a surveyed building location.
idScheme: proposedId = r16-lev-<slug> for region 9, r16-mes-<slug> for region 10, r16-irn-<slug> for region 11; the slug (key) is region-scoped to avoid homonyms. Stable, human-readable, non-canonical.
methodNote: Records are compiled from independent evidence (primary literary/administrative sources, archaeology/epigraphy and the Pleiades gazetteer for coordinates). Game/mod faction names are discovery leads only and never authorities. Every coordinate is a representative point with an explicit location confidence; where only a broad location is known the coordinate is coarse or null. Political authority is recorded only where supported; otherwise it is left unclaimed.
sourceAuditNote: Pleiades gazetteer identifiers are recorded only as 'to be confirmed', never asserted: automated access to pleiades.stoa.org was blocked by the site's anti-scraping protection during this pass, so no Pleiades id has been verified. Coordinates are approximate representative points, not surveyed locations or building footprints. All literary sources (Josephus, Strabo, Arrian, Diodorus, Polybius, Pliny, Ptolemy, the Babylonian astronomical diaries and other cuneiform records) are LATER than 278 BCE and are dated in each record; they are evidence for continuity, not contemporary snapshots. The 278 BCE horizon sits in the middle of the Syrian Wars: Ptolemy II holds Coele-Syria and Phoenicia and contests the Seleucid interior, so political control is often uncertain and must NOT be retrojected from later Hellenistic, Parthian, Roman, Sasanian or Islamic arrangements. Confirming Pleiades ids and coordinates manually remains an integration prerequisite.
politicalContext278Bce: Seleucid empire under Antiochus I (with his father Seleucus I newly dead in 281), centred on the Syrian tetrapolis (Antioch, Seleucia-in-Pieria, Apamea, Laodicea) and the eastern satrapies; Ptolemaic empire under Ptolemy II holds Coele-Syria/Phoenicia (southern Syria, the Phoenician coast, Judaea/Samaria and the Palestinian coast) and coastal Anatolia. The First and Second Syrian Wars (c.274-271, 260-253) are near or underway, so the Ptolemaic/Seleucid frontier in Syria is contested. The Nabataean kingdom is forming around Petra/Bostra; Judaea is a small temple-community (Yehud) under Ptolemaic rule. In the east, Babylon and Seleucia-on-the-Tigris are Seleucid royal seats and eastern Iran is held by Seleucid satraps even as local dynasties (e.g. Atropatene) and the Parthians are beginning to stir. Bactria/Sogdiana (region 12) are still under Seleucid control, NOT yet a Greco-Bactrian kingdom.
duplicateGuard: None of these records reproduce the 23 active atlas sites, the 12 deferred atlas candidates, the excluded site (Cosa), or any record of batches 1-2 (central Mediterranean, Greece/Aegean/Crete, Anatolia/Black Sea).
